Technology stocks fell during Monday trade, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing nearly 0.7% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was posting a 1.2% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) NeoPhotonics ( NPTN ) was 1.5% lower in late Monday trading after the optoelectronics company said it expects adjusted Q4 net income exceeding Wall Street estimates, projecting non-GAAP earnings between $0.00 to $0.04 per share. Analysts, on average, are looking for NeoPhotonics to report a $0.03 per share net loss for the three months ended Dec. 31
In other sector news:
(+) Camtek ( CAMT ) climbed as much as 6% on Monday after the semiconductor inspections company reaffirmed its Q4 outlook expecting between $32.5 million to $33.5 million in revenue, straddling the two-analyst estimate expecting $33 million for the three months ended Dec. 31.
(+) Maxar Technologies ( MAXR ) was 7% higher in recent trading after the networking equipment company named Daniel Jablonsky as its new CEO and president, succeeding Howard Lance who also stepped down as a board member in addition to resigning those positions.
(-) Western Digital ( WDC ) slumped Monday, falling almost 10% at one point, after Evercore ISI lowered its investment rating on the data-storage company's shares to underperform from in line.
